papers.title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries
papers.abstract_en: The pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries necessitates integration with next-generation high-voltage positive electrodes. However, a critical challenge lies in the intrinsic instability of most highly ionically conductive solid electrolytes, which decompose at potentials above 4.30 V vs Li+/Li, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and increased impedance. Here, we show that an amorphous Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 halide electrolyte, synthesized via a non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering strategy based on Li2ZrCl6, effectively overcomes this limitation. With a high ionic conductivity of 4.11 mS cm−1 at 25 °C, it enables stable high-potential cycling through kinetically stabilized operation mediated by a self-passivating positive electrode–electrolyte interphase. When paired with LiNi0.88Mn0.06Co0.06O2 positive electrode and a Li-In alloy negative electrode, the cells retain up to 81.2% of the initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C under cell cutoff voltages of 4.18 V (corresponding to 4.80 V vs Li⁺/Li). Overall, non-equimolar cation–anion amorphous engineering enables conductive, high-voltage-tolerant Zr-based halides for all-solid-state lithium batteries. High-voltage solid-state batteries require conductive, stable electrolytes for fast charging. Here, authors show that an amorphous Zr-based oxyhalide electrolyte combines high ionic conductivity with self-passivating interphases, enabling sustained cycling at high voltages.
papers.summary_ko: 비등몰비의 양이온-음이온 비정질화 전략으로 합성한 Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 할라이드 고체전해질이 4.11 mS/cm의 높은 이온전도도와 자기부동화(self-passivating) 계면 형성을 통해 4.3V 이상의 고전압에서도 안정적으로 작동함을 보였다. 고니켈 NCM 양극과 Li-In 합금 음극으로 구성한 전고체전지는 10C, 4.18V 컷오프 조건에서 2000회 사이클 후 81.2% 용량을 유지했다.

papers.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.
papers.summary_ko: 비할로겐계 설포모일-카보네이트 혼합 전해질을 개발하여 자기소화시간 약 0초의 불연성을 구현하고, 고전압 조건에서 리튬 금속 및 리튬이온전지 모두에서 안정적인 사이클링을 달성했다. 디메틸설파모일 플루오라이드와 FEC가 각각 양극과 음극(리튬 금속) 표면에 선제적으로 부동화층을 형성해 율속 특성, 저온 성능, 장기 사이클 안정성을 개선하며 열폭주 개시 온도를 87°C 지연시켰다.
